summary: Wood-timber wartime lookout built c.1943 with Army funds on the Monongahela; given to West Virginia in 1944; listed gone, exact site unknown.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no source says when it came down or what remains at the site
facts.agency: Built by the Monongahela National Forest; administered by the West Virginia Conservation Commission

events.note: Built with US Army funds (register gives 1943; Eastern US Lookouts gives c.1943)
Transferred to the State of West Virginia (register and Eastern US Lookouts); forest history gives 1944 and 1948 for the two wartime towers

evidence.supports: built 1943 by Monongahela National Forest with US Army funds; area used for Army training
evidence.quote: The tower was built in 1943 by Monongahela National Forest using US Army funds since the area was used for Army training.

evidence.supports: Army funding paid for three temporary towers, c.1943; Niges Cliff one of them; on North Mountain south of US 33
evidence.quote: c.1943: Army funding was used to construct three temporary lookout towers for fire protection, one of which was the Niges Cliff tower on the Potomac Ranger District south of U.S. Route 33 on North Mountain.

evidence.supports: extra land to protect while the Army trained in the area
evidence.quote: This tower was constructed primarily to protect the additional land the Forest Service was responsible for in the war years when the Army used the area for training purposes.

evidence.supports: forest history names two towers built with military funds, Niges Cliff and Pigeon Roost
evidence.quote: Two other fire towers were built in 1943 and 1944 using military funds associated with the WVMA: Niges Cliff Tower and Pigeons Roost Tower.

evidence.supports: one of a few towers built entirely of wood timbers
evidence.quote: a few, like Bearden Knob, Niges Cliff, Pigeons Roost towers, were constructed entirely of wood timbers

evidence.supports: register places the tower along North Fork Mountain; exact location unknown
evidence.quote: This tower was located along North Fork Mountain. Its exact location is unknown.

evidence.supports: register gives coordinates in Pendleton County
register gives 1944 transfer to the State of West Virginia
evidence.quote: The tower was transferred to the State of West Virginia in 1944.
1944: The Niges Cliff lookout was transferred to the State of West Virginia.

evidence.supports: forest history gives 1944 and 1948 for the two towers, without naming which
evidence.quote: The USDA Forest Service transferred ownership of these two fire towers to the State of West Virginia in 1944 and 1948.

evidence.supports: administered by the West Virginia Conservation Commission
evidence.quote: Administered by West Virginia Conservation Commission

evidence.supports: FFLA list shows the tower gone with coordinates unknown
evidence.quote: Niges Cliff Pendleton Unknown Tower Gone FFLOS US 1640, WV 31

evidence.supports: most towers on the forest were simply razed
evidence.quote: Most, however, were simply razed, leaving only their concrete piers and steps as the evidence of their existence.

corrections.why: Capitalization typo in 'SIte'; the register heading repeats the typo
Transferred to the State of West Virginia in 1944, and the register lists the West Virginia Conservation Commission as administrator
The register says its exact location is unknown, and the FFLA list shows the coordinates as Unknown

sources.title: Niges Cliff Tower Site, Former Fire Lookout Sites register entry US 1640
Monongahela National Forest fire towers history (PDF)

notes_for_editor: The register (North Fork Mountain, exact location unknown) and Eastern US Lookouts (North Mountain, south of US 33) disagree on the ridge; the register also lists coordinates, which conflicts with its own 'exact location is unknown' line. Do not present the point as a precise site. Forest Fire Lookout Association's North Fork Mountain entry (US 164, Pendleton) is a different tower. Army-funded tower count: Eastern says three, the forest history names two (Niges Cliff, Pigeon Roost). No staffing, fire or access history found in sources read; access left out. Eastern US Lookouts is a long index page; quotes come from its Niges Cliff section.
